host_galaxy.comment:
Hjorth+2012: TOUGH Table 3 identified host. Redshift note='\\nodata', reference(s)='\\nodata'; E/AE/AE* denote host emission-line redshifts, A/A* afterglow absorption spectroscopy, and P afterglow photometric redshift. Host R/Ks magnitudes are observed Vega magnitudes, uncorrected for foreground extinction; upper-limit confidence levels were not stated.
Perley+2013: Perley+2013 Tables 1–2 identified host; Redshift method as published: host_photometric. Host coordinates use the RAH/DEH columns, not the afterglow RAJ2000/DEJ2000 columns. Table 3 magnitudes are uncorrected for foreground Galactic extinction; measurement errors are 1 sigma. Figure 3 describes the upper limits as 2 sigma. Table 4 photometric-redshift 95% uncertainty: lower=-0.52, upper=+0.58; redshift_err remains null because AJST cannot represent asymmetric errors. Redshift provenance: Tables 1–2/CDS give z=2.6; Table 4 gives 2.50 (+0.58/-0.52), and Section 5 gives EaZy best-fit 2.47 with 95% range 1.98–3.08. The Tables 1–2 value is used here without hiding the difference.
Hjorth+2012: Source access: arXiv v2 Table 3 TeX was used after the IOP VoR/MRT route was blocked; this is a documented substitution.
Merged-field decision: host coordinates taken from Hjorth+2012 according to the direct-measurement priority rule.
Merged-field decision: redshift, error, and type taken as one tuple from Perley+2013 according to the recency/method priority rule.
